verdict.line: You lose this if you trade into Ornn's ranged Q poke for stacks and get caught against a wall for his E combo; you win it if you farm safe to level 6+, bank Q stacks, and all-in with R while his E and R are down.

brief.thesis: Nasus overall sits at 51.2% in this role, but drops to 45.5% over 88 games specifically against Ornn, and the reason is range and tempo: Ornn's Q (Volcanic Rupture, 800 range) out-pokes your Q (Siphoning Strike, 255 range) every single cooldown rotation while his passive (Living Forge) bonus resists make early trades worse than they look. The matchup flips once you're past level 6 with real Q stacks, because Fury of the Sands turns you into the all-in threat and Ornn has no way to peel once Wither is on him.

theirWindow.when: his Q slow lands near a wall
theirWindow.what: Volcanic Rupture slows on hit and drops a pillar after a delay — if you're slowed anywhere near terrain, Searing Charge (14/13.5/13/12.5/12s cd) can collide with that terrain for a knockup, then W's final gout of flame applies Brittle before he unloads. Walk away from walls the instant his Q is thrown, don't just dodge the initial hit.

yourWindow.when: level 6+ with Q stacks and his E/R down
yourWindow.what: Once Fury of the Sands is up, land Wither first to tank his Move and Attack Speed, then walk in and chain Siphoning Strike — he has no dash if Searing Charge is on cooldown and no knockup reset if Call of the Forge God (140/120/100/100/100s cd) isn't ready.

start.why: 68.5% pick rate here for a reason — the sustain and poke-damage reduction directly answer Ornn's ranged Q harass while you farm Q stacks.

boots.why: 57.7% pick, 41.7% win rate — the extra ability haste lowers Wither and Spirit Fire cooldowns, which matters more here than raw magic resist since Ornn's combo isn't primarily auto-attack damage.

core.why: the most-run first core item (46.2% win rate path) — the stats let you actually win trades once you commit, instead of just farming stacks passively.
armor and ability haste blunt his Q poke and Searing Charge follow-ups while keeping your own cooldowns low.
magic resist plus healing amp directly counters Ornn's magic damage kit and stacks with your Soul Eater lifesteal.

runes.keystoneWhy: it heals and gives move speed off basic attacks, not spells, so it directly rewards farming Q stacks and absorbing his ranged Q poke instead of punishing you for playing passively.

summoners.why: the highest-picked combo (53.7% pick) — Teleport lets you reset onto lane after back-and-forth poke exchanges without losing stacking time, and Ghost closes the gap for your post-6 all-in since you have no other gap closer.

playing.title: Farm Q stacks, don't trade for them
playing.detail: Take Siphoning Strike on minions whenever it's free; don't walk up into his 800-range Q just to get a stack, since he wins that exchange every time pre-6.

playing.title: Stay off walls when his Q is up
playing.detail: Volcanic Rupture's pillar plus a nearby wall is what lets Searing Charge knock you up — if you're slowed, move away from terrain immediately rather than trying to dodge.

playing.title: Drop Spirit Fire after he commits Q
playing.detail: Spirit Fire's armor reduction is wasted if he's still at range; throw it once he's walked in to poke so the armor shred actually lands during the trade.

playing.title: Hold Wither for his engage, not his poke
playing.detail: Wither decelerates Move and Attack Speed over time, so it's far more valuable locking him down mid-Searing Charge or mid-fight than chip-damaging him at range.

playing.title: All-in only with R and stacks both up
playing.detail: Fury of the Sands is a 120s cooldown — don't burn it to just poke. Wait until you have it plus a meaningful Q stack count and his Call of the Forge God is down.

playing.title: Don't play recall timers against him
playing.detail: Living Forge lets Ornn build items without backing, so he won't give you free waves from recalls the way other laners do — win priority through wave management instead.

playing.title: Respect the W engage range
playing.detail: Bellows Breath lets him advance in while breathing fire, and the final gout applies Brittle — don't stand still at max range assuming you're safe from the follow-up.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate numbers above are measured from real games on the current patch (16.20.1) via OP.GG; the tactical reasoning — why the poke war favors him early and why R plus stacks flips it — is my own read on the mechanics, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: It is important to avoid Ornn’s (Q)-(E) combo. Focus foremost on raising your [Q] stacks, and try go in for the kill post-level 6 when Unsealed Spellbook + Fury of the Sands [R] come off cooldown.
